A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TALE framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA evaluations, human-annotator agreement, iteration and query-generation ablations, and evaluation case studies in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluated baselines, prompt-variation experiments, query-drift measurements, and a cost analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the default module prompts retain the same query, search, summarization, reflection, memory, and judgment procedure. The new baseline and prompt variants are experimental controls. Adaptive stopping and credibility weighting are proposed as future work, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AmbigQA, HotpotQA, NQ-Open, TriviaQA, and FreshQA. The added comparisons and analyses use existing tasks and samples; they introduce no distinct dataset, population, domain, or task requirement.

E2.justification: Appendix C.1 and Table 9 add three evaluated comparators: a single-pass tool judge without summarization/reflection/refinement, a self-consistency judge, and majority voting across GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, and Mistral 7B. These substantially extend v1's comparisons. PoLL and DAFE inspire the ensemble baseline but are not themselves newly evaluated implementations.

E3.justification: The original sampling and metrics remain unchanged, but Appendix C adds substantial experimental designs: ten-verdict voting at temperature 0.7, single-search and model-ensemble controls, zero-/one-/three-shot prompt comparisons, and query-level sufficiency coding across the existing 100 error cases. These are protocols for added experiments, not revisions to the original benchmark settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls examining tool access versus the full iterative pipeline, prompt robustness tests, a quantitative query-drift audit, and computational cost analysis. The original iteration and query-removal ablations remain, and the existing failure cases move from B.5 to C.3 rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 newly reports rerunning the default prompt and reproducing the previous kappa and Macro-F1 scores. No seed schedule, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added. The ten verdicts in self-consistency are a voting procedure, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The original numerical results are retained. New Table 9 reports single-pass kappa of 0.658/0.583 and ensemble kappa of 0.609/0.527 on AmbigQA/HotpotQA. Table 10 adds prompt-specific results; Table 16 adds query-drift counts; Section 5.4 reports $0.00216 and 27 seconds per item. These are additional findings under specified settings, not improved versions of the original scores.

T1.justification: The substantive algorithmic equations and metric definitions remain equivalent. Section 3.2 removes redundant judge formalization whose behavior remains specified in Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about reference-free evaluation and human agreement remain unchanged. The introduction drops the ablation study as a separately listed contribution, reducing four explicit contributions to three, although the ablations themselves remain and expand.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains reliance on cross-source agreement without credibility scoring, proposes adaptive stopping, and discusses latency and resource tradeoffs for offline evaluation. It also interprets the new prompt and comparator results. Much of the discussion of model capability, context limits, and conflicting evidence already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: Section 5.4 newly documents token consumption, latency, and pricing assumptions. Appendix C specifies the added controls' sampling, model membership, and prompt-example counts. It also promises release of retrieved snippets and domains; the PDF does not establish a completed release. Existing default prompts and implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 expands discussion of the already cited Agent-as-a-Judge and emphasizes objective verdicts versus subjective scores. v2 adds Xuezhi Wang et al.'s self-consistency paper and removes Kamalloo et al.'s QA-evaluation paper and Cunxiang Wang et al.'s Evaluating Open-QA Evaluation. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and method explanations are condensed, contributions become an inline list, and acknowledgments are removed. Failure cases move from B.5 to C.3, alongside separate limitations and ethics appendices. These are localized editorial and organizational changes; most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9, 10, and 16. Figure 1 is made more compact and gains an explicit judge label; Figure 2 changes sizing, legends, and axis presentation while retaining its trends. Existing tables are relocated or renumbered, and the final case study's explanation moves into its caption.

improvement.justification: The added comparator and prompt experiments strengthen support for iterative evaluation on the existing human-annotated tasks, while cost reporting improves practical transparency. The gains are useful but incremental and include small reporting defects: Table 16's third-query counts total 99 despite claiming 100, and Table 10 shows a 3.2-point kappa drop where the prose claims at most three points. These issues limit, but do not outweigh, the added evidence.
